title: Enone + R2CuLi → 1,4 (conjugate) addition
why: Cuprates are soft nucleophiles, so they add to the soft β-carbon (1,4) rather than the C=O carbon. The enolate that forms is protonated on workup and tautomerizes back to the ketone, now carrying a methyl at the β-position.

traps.explains: That's 1,2-addition, which is what a hard nucleophile like CH3MgBr or CH3Li does. Cuprates add 1,4.
The methyl lands on the β-carbon (two carbons from C=O), not the α-carbon next to it.
Cuprates don't reduce the C=O. After workup the ketone is still there.

review: Arrows show the simplified 'carbanion adds to β-carbon' picture, not the Cu(III) oxidative-addition mechanism. Check this is acceptable as the drilled key step (it is the standard textbook simplification).
